## Overview

The `ternary` plugin converts a full-precision checkpoint into a **ternary** model — every
transformer-block weight becomes one of `{-1, 0, +1}` times a per-tensor scale, about
1.58 bits per weight — and heals the damage with continued training. The result is
exported to formats that run today: a bf16 "master" checkpoint, transformers' packed
BitNet layout, GGUF `TQ2_0`/`TQ1_0` for llama.cpp, `I2_S` for bitnet.cpp, and a
sparsity-adaptive `mask_sign` archive that costs `2 − zero_fraction` bits per weight.

This is the *conversion* path. If you already have a prequantized BitNet checkpoint (the
Falcon-E series) and only want to fine-tune it, see
[1.58-bit Finetuning](1_58bit_finetuning.qmd) instead — the two are mutually exclusive.

::: {.callout-important}
Conversion is a full fine-tune. Adapters (`adapter: lora`/`qlora`) and every other
quantization path (`use_onebitllms`, `qat:`, `quantization:`, `load_in_8bit`,
`load_in_4bit`) are rejected: the latent weights need dense gradients, and the ternary
quantizer owns the weight representation for the whole run.
:::

## How it works

**1. Swap.** After the model is built and weights are loaded — but before any FSDP or
DeepSpeed wrapping — each targeted `nn.Linear` is replaced by a `TernaryLinear`. Matching
is by regex against `named_modules()` names, and it is *strict*: every `nn.Linear` in the
model must fullmatch exactly one of `target_modules` or `keep_fp_modules`. An unmatched or
doubly-matched module is a hard error, not a warning. This is what stops an unanchored
`.*gate.*` pattern from quietly ternarizing a MoE router.

Embeddings, `lm_head` and all norms are never ternarized, regardless of what your regexes
say. Quantizing them destroys the model and no deployment format expects it.

**2. Heal.** `TernaryLinear` does fake quantization on every forward: weights are rounded
to codes against a per-tensor absmean scale, activations to per-token int8, and a
straight-through estimator sends gradients back into the bf16 latent weights. Quantization
is faded in with a λ warmup

$$w_\text{eff} = w + \lambda \cdot (w_q - w), \qquad \lambda = \min(\text{step} / \text{warmup}, 1)$$

so the model is never shocked into ternary. Weight decay is annealed to zero partway
through the run, because decay keeps flipping ternary code assignments and prevents them
from settling.

**3. Bake and export.** At save time the latents are replaced in place by exact
`{-s, 0, +s}` bf16 values — the "master" checkpoint — and the packers re-derive codes from
it. The dequantized value uses the scale *rounded through fp16*, which is what makes the
master re-quantize to identical codes in every downstream packer instead of drifting by a
code here and there.

## Quickstart

```yaml
base_model: meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B

plugins:
  - axolotl.integrations.ternary.TernaryPlugin

ternary:
  lambda_warmup_steps: 1000
  export:
    formats: [master_bf16, hf_bitnet]

pretraining_dataset:
  - path: HuggingFaceFW/fineweb-edu
    name: sample-10BT
    type: pretrain
    split: train
streaming: true

sequence_len: 2048
sample_packing: true
max_steps: 20000

learning_rate: 1e-4
lr_scheduler: cosine
weight_decay: 0.01
save_only_model: true
bf16: true
```

```bash
axolotl train config.yaml
```

Healing is continued pretraining, so feed it raw text (`pretraining_dataset` or packed
completion data), not instruction data with masked prompts. A learning rate around `1e-4`
with cosine decay is the documented starting point.

::: {.callout-tip}
`save_only_model: true` is recommended. Optimizer state for a run that is being baked to a
ternary master is dead weight in every checkpoint.
:::

## Token budget expectations

Conversion is not free. The published evidence is consistent about what a given budget
buys:

| Budget | Outcome |
|---|---|
| ~0 (PTQ only) | ~90% retention at 27B+; weak below 8B |
| ~1B tokens | demo quality |
| ~10B tokens | usable model; task-parity with distillation at ≤4B |
| ~30B+ tokens | good general model |
| ~100B tokens | approaches, but does not match, the FP16 base at 8B without a teacher |

Budget the run before starting it. A 1B-token heal of an 8B model produces something that
talks, not something you ship.

## Configuration reference

All options live under the `ternary:` key.

### Module selection

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `target_modules` | preset | Regexes fullmatched against module names; each match becomes a `TernaryLinear`. Defaults to the architecture preset. |
| `keep_fp_modules` | preset | Regexes for Linears that stay full precision. |
| `strict_enumeration` | `true` | Require every `nn.Linear` to fullmatch exactly one list. `false` downgrades unmatched/double-matched modules to a warning and keeps them FP. |

Presets exist for `llama` and `qwen3` dense architectures and target
`.*\.self_attn\.(q|k|v|o)_proj` plus `.*\.mlp\.(gate|up|down)_proj`. Other architectures
need explicit `target_modules`.

### Quantizer

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `weight_scale` | `absmean` | `absmean` (per-tensor statistic), `group` (per `group_size` block), `learnable` (per-tensor scale trained jointly), `learnable_row` (one trained scale per output channel), `dual` (five values `{0, ±s_lo, ±s_hi}` from two trained per-row scales), `trit_planes` (PTQTP-style free sum of two trit planes — per row two scales `s1 >= s2` and per weight two trits, `w = t1·s1 + t2·s2`, spanning up to nine values `{0, ±s2, ±(s1−s2), ±s1, ±(s1+s2)}`). `absmean` and `learnable` are per-tensor and export everywhere; the rest are `master_bf16` only. |
| `group_size` | `null` | Block size for `weight_scale: group`, at least 32 (128 or 256 are the usual values). Required with it, rejected with every other mode. |
| `activation_bits` | `8` | `8` for per-token int8 activation quantization, `null` for weight-only QAT. |
| `init` | `absmean` | Latent initialization for the swapped modules: `absmean` (leave the FP weights alone), `ternary_fit` (data-free alternating scale/state solve), `ternary_fit_calibrated` (activation-aware refit plus error compensation over `init_calibration` sequences). `svid` is planned. Everything but `absmean` requires a scale-keeping `weight_scale` — see [Initialization](#initialization). |
| `init_jitter` | `0.0` | Gaussian noise added to the latent after a fitting init, as a multiple of the module's quantization step (the finer of the pair under `dual`/`trit_planes`). Requires a fitting init; deterministic from `seed` and the module name. |
| `smoothing` | `false` | *Planned.* Fold a SmoothQuant-style norm→linear rescale into the weights before the swap. |
| `subln` | `false` | Insert BitDistill-style sub-norms before `o_proj`/`down_proj`. Changes the architecture: the norms are saved into the bf16 master, which then only reloads through this plugin, and no packed format has a tensor slot for them — `hf_bitnet` included, so `export.formats` has to be `master_bf16` (optionally with `mask_sign`). |

Under `ternary.init_calibration`, read only by `init: ternary_fit_calibrated`:

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `num_sequences` | `128` | Sequences the layer-wise Gram matrices are accumulated over. 128 is the published operating point for GPTQ-family solvers. |
| `sequence_len` | `2048` | Tokens per calibration sequence; longer ones are truncated. |
| `dataset` | `null` | Dataset to calibrate on. `null` uses the training dataset, which is what you want: calibrating on a corpus that does not match the healing corpus costs more perplexity than the whole method buys. |

Setting the block under any other `init` is a config error rather than a silently ignored
knob.

::: {.callout-note}
`trit_planes` stores ~4.25 bpw against the single plane's ~1.58, which puts it in the
research/ablation tier rather than the deployment one: two planes are what buys the extra
levels, and no packed format has a slot for the second. It is master-only by validation,
and its scales round through the master's dtype rather than f16 — a *sum* of two scales
only lands back on the stored value if both are already exact there.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
The schema accepts `init: svid` and `smoothing: true`, but nothing implements them yet, so
the plugin raises `NotImplementedError` rather than training a model that silently ignored
them.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
`weight_scale: group`, `learnable_row`, `dual` and `trit_planes` cannot be exported to `hf_bitnet`,
`gguf_tq2_0`, `gguf_tq1_0`, `i2_s` or `mask_sign` — those formats carry a single per-tensor
scale and a single trit plane. Those modes are `master_bf16` only, and the config validator
will tell you so up front rather than at export time.
:::

### Initialization {#initialization}

A fit writes the solver's own reconstruction into the latent, which leaves every weight
at a cell centre — half a quantization step from the nearest assignment boundary. No
optimizer step small enough to be stable moves a weight that far, so the codes stay frozen
at the solver's output for the whole heal and the run trains only scales and norms;
`ternary/flip_rate` reads a flat zero, which is the symptom to watch for.
`init_jitter: 0.25` restores the distance-to-boundary spread the fit removed, so use it
whenever a fitting init is paired with a conservative learning rate. It also gives the
merge/ensemble recipe something to average: two seeds jitter differently, so their heals
explore different assignments rather than converging on the one the solver picked.

`init: absmean` starts the heal from the original FP weights and lets the quantizer round
them at step 0. The fitting modes instead rewrite each latent so that its *quantized* form
is already the best ternary approximation of the original tensor:

- **`ternary_fit`** — data-free. A closed-form symmetric scale solve alternated with the
  optimal 3-state assignment, ~30 iterations per tensor. Costs nothing but CPU time and
  needs no corpus.
- **`ternary_fit_calibrated`** — `ternary_fit` plus an activation-aware refit against
  `S = XᵀX` accumulated over `init_calibration` sequences, inside a GPTQ-style
  error-compensation loop, one decoder layer at a time. The published ablations put most of
  the gain in the activation-weighted refit rather than the data-free part.

Both write the fit's own reconstruction — `codes · s` — into the latent, which has two
consequences worth knowing before you turn one on:

::: {.callout-important}
A fitting `init` requires a `weight_scale` that **keeps** the scale it solved:
`learnable`, `learnable_row` or `dual`. `absmean` and `group` re-derive their scale from
the latent on every forward, and `absmean(codes · s)` is `s` times the non-zero code
fraction — so the solve would survive exactly until the first optimizer step, after which
the model is a *worse* approximation than `init: absmean` ever was. The config validator
rejects that pair. `learnable` is per-tensor and exports everywhere, so it is the drop-in
for `absmean`.
:::

The λ warmup also has nothing left to walk to: the latent already *is* the quantized
weight, so `fake_quant` is the identity and every λ produces the same forward. Pair a
fitting init with `lambda_schedule: none` (the validator warns otherwise) and spend the
budget on the heal instead.

Neither replaces healing. Pure PTQ to ternary is weak below ~8B and collapses on
data-saturated models; a fitted init buys a head start, not a shipped model. Measure it —
run the [damage map](#damage-map) before and compare the `weights` row. The damage map
itself always swaps with `init: absmean` and `subln: false`, whatever the config says, so
its baseline stays the untouched FP model.

### Schedules

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `lambda_schedule` | `linear` | How λ ramps 0 → 1: `linear`, `sigmoid`, or `none` (quantize at full strength from step 0). |
| `lambda_warmup_steps` | `1000` | λ warmup length. The **type** decides: an int is an absolute step count, a float in `(0, 1]` is a fraction of `max_steps` — so `1` means one step and `1.0` means the whole run. |
| `weight_decay_zero_at` | `0.5` | Fraction of training after which weight decay is annealed to 0. `1.0` keeps decay for the whole run. |

`linear` is the default because it is the only schedule with clear published evidence
behind it; discrete jumps to λ=1 fail.

### Performance

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `int8_forward` | `auto` | Use the int8 tensor-core W2A8 forward once λ reaches 1. `auto` enables it when shapes and hardware qualify, and falls back silently otherwise. |
| `fused_fake_quant` | `true` | Use the fused Triton fake-quant kernels instead of the eager reference implementation. |
| `share_act_quant` | `false` | Quantize a shared input once for every linear that consumes it (`q`/`k`/`v`, `gate`/`up`) instead of once per linear. |

### Monitoring

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `log_code_flip_every` | `100` | Log ternary code-flip rate and zero fraction every N steps; `0` disables monitoring and its packed-code snapshot buffers. |

Two metrics per module family (`q_proj`, `down_proj`, …) land in your trainer logs. They
go through the trainer's metric store, so they reach the trackers (W&B, TensorBoard, MLflow)
and `state.log_history`, not just the console. Under FSDP2 each rank measures its own shard,
so the numbers are per-rank:

- `ternary/flip_rate/<family>` — fraction of codes that changed since the last snapshot.
  Near zero means the codes are frozen (LR too low, or the run is done); sustained high
  means thrashing (LR too high).
- `ternary/zero_frac/<family>` — fraction of codes that are `0`. A family collapsing toward
  all-zero is a dead layer.

### Distillation

Under `ternary.distill`:

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `mode` | `null` | `null` (pure QAT), `kd_plugin` (compose with the KD integration), `inprocess` (frozen teacher loaded beside the student). |
| `teacher_model` | `base_model` | Teacher checkpoint. Defaults to the unquantized base you are converting. |
| `teacher_device_map` | `null` | `device_map` for the `inprocess` teacher (e.g. `auto`, `cpu`) so a teacher that does not fit beside the student can be offloaded. |
| `logits_weight` | `0.5` | Mixing coefficient between CE and logits-KD: `(1 - w)·CE + w·τ²·KL`. Must be in `[0, 1]`. Pure KD (`1.0`) matches the teacher's temperature-flattened tails at the expense of head sharpness — on short heals it measures better on teacher-KL but worse on perplexity than the CE blend, so reserve it for long OneBit-style distillation runs. |
| `logits_temperature` | `2.0` | Softmax temperature for the logits-KD term. |
| `hidden_weight` | `0.0` | Hidden-state feature-KD weight. `inprocess` only; `0` disables. Retune it when changing `hidden_loss` — the variants are on different scales. |
| `hidden_loss` | `cosine` | How the hidden-state term compares the two residual streams. `cosine` matches direction only, ignoring the outlier channels that dominate a residual stream (TernaryLLM's OFF result; OneBit's normalized MSE is the same objective). `mse` is raw MSE on the unnormalized hidden states — magnitude-aware, which is the case for it, since those magnitudes set the mixing ratio between blocks, but a few outlier channels then dominate the gradient. `huber` keeps the magnitude sensitivity with outlier influence bounded. |
| `hidden_huber_delta` | `1.0` | Elbow of `hidden_loss: huber`, in hidden-state units. Only valid with `huber`. |
| `attn_relation_layer` | `null` | *Experimental.* Layer index for single-layer attention-relation KD. `inprocess` only; negative indexes count from the last layer. Results are sensitive to the layer choice. |
| `schedule` | `constant` | When the KD term contributes: `constant` blends it across the whole run, `anchored` switches it on only for the last `1 - anchor_start` of the steps. |
| `anchor_start` | `0.9` | Fraction of `max_steps` after which `schedule: anchored` turns the KD term on. Ignored under `constant`. |

**Why `anchored`.** The only public conversion at 8B with ~96% benchmark retention runs a
CE-dominant QAT phase and then turns KD on *only* for the LR-decay tail — the teacher
anchors the model where the learning rate can no longer move it far, instead of pulling on
it for the whole run. It is also cheaper: with an in-process teacher, 90% of the steps skip
the teacher forward entirely. `constant` remains the default because it is the
better-documented setting; `anchored` is the A/B worth running on a real budget.

Requesting `schedule: anchored` without a `distill.mode` is a config error — there would be
no KD term to anchor.

### Export

Under `ternary.export`:

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `formats` | `[master_bf16, hf_bitnet]` | Artifacts written after training completes. |
| `run_parity_gate` | `true` | Verify each packed export against the baked master and fail the export when it does not match. |
| `embedding_dtype` | `bf16` | Weight dtype for the token embeddings and the output head (one tensor when tied). `int8` packs them as Q8_0 — 32 weights per block with an f16 scale, ~8.5 bpw against 16. Unembedding is 40%+ of decode DRAM traffic on a ternary model, where every other weight is already ~2 bpw, and int8 weight-only embeddings are near-lossless. |

::: {.callout-note}
`embedding_dtype: int8` is a GGUF-only option. `master_bf16` always keeps full-precision
embeddings — it is the re-finetunable interchange artifact — and `hf_bitnet` has no scheme
for quantized ones. Setting it with no GGUF format in `formats` is a config error; with a
mix, the GGUF artifacts get int8 embeddings and the others are logged as exempt.
:::

## Teacher options

**No teacher (`distill.mode: null`).** Pure QAT on next-token loss. Simplest, cheapest per
step, and the recipe the token-budget table above is calibrated for. Start here.

**`distill.mode: kd_plugin`.** Compose with axolotl's existing
[KD integration](https://github.com/axolotl-ai-cloud/axolotl/tree/main/src/axolotl/integrations/kd):
serve the FP base with [`axolotl vllm-serve`](vllm_serving.qmd) or precompute an offline
top-k logprob dataset, and run the KD trainer against the swapped model. This is the
memory-cheap path and the recommendation for teachers at 7B and above, since the teacher
never has to sit in the training process.

**`distill.mode: inprocess`.** A frozen copy of `teacher_model` is loaded beside the
student and runs under `no_grad` in eval mode. The loss is cross-entropy plus a chunked
logits-KD term (computed per vocab-chunk so a 128k+ vocabulary does not blow up memory),
optionally plus cosine hidden-state KD and single-layer attention-relation KD. Use it for
teachers up to ~4B, or on boxes with GPUs to spare.

```yaml
ternary:
  distill:
    mode: inprocess
    logits_weight: 0.5
    logits_temperature: 2.0
    hidden_weight: 0.1
```

## Export formats

Exports listed in `ternary.export.formats` are written automatically when training
finishes. You can also produce them later from a saved master:

```bash
axolotl ternary export config.yaml --format gguf_tq2_0 --format i2_s
axolotl ternary export config.yaml --format hf_bitnet --output-dir ./exports
```

`--format` is repeatable and defaults to `ternary.export.formats`; `--output-dir` defaults
to the config's `output_dir`, which is also where the baked master is read from.

| Format | Bits/weight | Runtime |
|---|---|---|
| `master_bf16` | 16 | transformers, and any axolotl run — this is the refinetunable interchange artifact |
| `hf_bitnet` | 2.0 | transformers `BitNetForCausalLM` |
| `gguf_tq2_0` | 2.0625 | llama.cpp |
| `gguf_tq1_0` | 1.6875 | llama.cpp |
| `i2_s` | 2.0 | bitnet.cpp |
| `mask_sign` | `2 − zero_fraction` | none (archival/transport; unpack with this plugin) |
| `onebitllms_bf16` | 16 | axolotl's `use_onebitllms: true` finetuning path (`BitNetLinear` re-derives its own grid; see [Continuing training with onebitllms](#onebitllms)) |

::: {.callout-note}
GGUF exports (`gguf_tq2_0`, `gguf_tq1_0`, `i2_s`) require the optional `gguf` package:
`uv pip install gguf`.
:::

### master_bf16

A normal bf16 checkpoint whose weight values happen to be exactly `{-s, 0, +s}`. Loads
with `AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained` and can be fine-tuned further — every packed
format is derived from it, so nothing is lost by keeping it around.

Loading one back through the plugin is a fixed point: the swap detects that the weights
are already on the ternary grid and recovers `s` from their `amax`, so the reloaded model
computes exactly what the saved one did. (Re-running the absmean quantizer on ternary
values would shrink every weight by the non-zero code fraction.)

### hf_bitnet

Packs four ternary codes per `uint8` (`code + 1` at bit shifts `[0, 2, 4, 6]`, tensor shape
`(out_features / 4, in_features)`), stores a scalar `weight_scale` per tensor, and stamps
`quantization_config: {quant_method: bitnet}` into `config.json`:

```python
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer

model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("./outputs/ternary-out/hf_bitnet")
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("./outputs/ternary-out/hf_bitnet")
```

### gguf_tq2_0 / gguf_tq1_0

Upstream llama.cpp ternary block types. `TQ2_0` is the faster of the two and the one to
reach for first; `TQ1_0` trades speed for ~0.4 bits per weight. Embeddings and the output
head are written as Q6_K/F16.

```bash
llama-cli -m ./outputs/ternary-out/model-tq2_0.gguf -p "Hello"
```

::: {.callout-note}
You cannot `llama-quantize` a normal FP model into `TQ2_0`/`TQ1_0`. The source has to
already be ternary-with-scale — which is exactly what the baked master is.
:::

### i2_s

The GGUF variant bitnet.cpp's CPU runtime consumes:

```bash
python setup_env.py -md ./outputs/ternary-out -q i2_s
python run_inference.py -m ./outputs/ternary-out/ggml-model-i2_s.gguf -p "Hello"
```

### onebitllms_bf16 {#onebitllms}

A full checkpoint directory — config, tokenizer and all — whose ternary tensors are
stored *inflated*. It exists to hand a healed model to axolotl's existing
`use_onebitllms: true` path for further finetuning.

`onebitllms`' `BitNetLinear` is a QAT layer, not a loader: it keeps a full-precision
latent and re-derives its own b1.58 grid on every forward,

```
scale = 1 / max(mean|w|, 1e-5),   codes = round(w · scale).clamp(±1),   w_eff = codes / scale
```

so a checkpoint hands it a *latent*, not a grid. **Do not point `use_onebitllms` at the
raw master.** The master holds `code · s`, whose absmean is `s · (1 − z)` for a zero
fraction `z`, so their scale comes out `1 / (s · (1 − z))`: the codes survive, but every
weight dequantizes to `code · s · (1 − z)`. At the ~33% density a healed model settles
at, that is a uniform **0.68x shrink of every linear** — measured end to end against
real `BitNetLinear`, a 1-layer model already drifts 14% in max logit, and the error
compounds with depth.

This format applies the closed-form fix: store `code · s / (1 − z)`. Then `mean|w| = s`
exactly, their scale is `1 / s`, their codes are `round(code / (1 − z)).clamp(±1)` — which
is `code` for every `z` in `[0, 1)`, since `1 / (1 − z) >= 1` — and their dequant is
`code · s`. The trained function is an exact fixed point of their quantizer. The
per-tensor factors land in `ternary_onebitllms.json` beside the shards, and the export's
parity gate re-runs their quantizer over the written tensors, so the raw-master mistake
fails the gate rather than shipping.

Per-tensor single-plane scale modes only (`absmean`, `learnable`): `BitNetLinear`
re-derives one scale for the whole tensor, so a group, per-row or two-plane grid has
nowhere to live. `subln` is refused for the same reason —
`replace_linear_with_bitnet_linear` swaps stock `nn.Linear` modules and has no slot for
the inserted sub-norm.

The handoff, end to end:

```yaml
# 1. convert and heal, exporting the bridge format
plugins:
  - axolotl.integrations.ternary.TernaryPlugin
ternary:
  weight_scale: absmean
  export:
    formats: [master_bf16, onebitllms_bf16]
```

```yaml
# 2. continue training from the export — the ternary plugin is NOT used here;
#    `use_onebitllms` owns the weight representation and the two are mutually exclusive
base_model: ./outputs/ternary-out/onebitllms_bf16
use_onebitllms: true
```

Then `onebitllms`' own `quantize_to_1bit` produces their packed artifact from whatever
that run saves.

::: {.callout-warning}
`replace_linear_with_bitnet_linear` swaps *every* `nn.Linear` except `lm_head`. If your
run kept some block Linear in full precision through `ternary.keep_fp_modules`, the
finetune will quantize it anyway and will not match the exported function on that
module; the exporter logs a warning listing them.
:::

### mask_sign

This plugin's own packing, and the only format whose size depends on the model rather than
the format. Each tensor becomes a header, a 1-bit-per-weight zero bitmap, and one sign bit
per *nonzero* weight — so the payload costs `2 − zero_fraction` bits per weight instead of a
flat 2.0, plus a 32-byte header carrying the shape, the nonzero count and the f16 scale. The
packed byte strings live in an ordinary safetensors container under
`<module>.weight_mask_sign`, beside a `ternary_mask_sign.json` that records each tensor's
shape, nonzero count, measured bits per weight and sha256.

**Prefer it when your healed model is sparse.** Plain absmean rounding lands near a 33%
zero fraction, where this saves little (~1.67 bpw). The strongest published conversions
settle nearer 60%, where it costs ~1.4 bpw — below `TQ1_0`, with no block structure and no
codebook. `ternary/zero_frac/<family>` in your training logs says which regime you are in
before you bother.

**It is not a kernel format.** Decoding a weight means a prefix sum over the mask, not a
shift, so no runtime consumes it directly; it is for archiving and shipping checkpoints
whose sparsity you paid for. Per-tensor scale only, like the other packed formats.

### Parity gates

With `run_parity_gate: true` (the default), every export is checked against the master
before it is accepted:

1. **Exact code equality** — the codes recovered from the artifact must match the codes
   re-derived from the master, with zero mismatches. This is achievable because the master
   dequantizes with an fp16-rounded scale, so every packer's block scale reproduces it.
2. **Dequant error bound** — the maximum absolute difference must stay within the fp16
   rounding error of the scale.
3. **Weight-path smoke eval** — fixed-prompt logits from the artifact's decoded weights
   against the master's, with the *same* activation quantizer on both sides. That makes it
   a deterministic graph fed bit-identical weights, so the delta is 0 and a layout
   transpose or an inverted scale blows it up.
4. **Runtime-quantizer equivalence** — the deployment activation quantizer (for
   `hf_bitnet`, BitLinear's: it floors `amax` where training floors the scale) is compared
   to the training one *directly*, on the real pre-linear activations captured from the
   reference forward: the fraction of int8 codes that disagree, the largest disagreement
   in scale steps, and the extreme codes both reach.

The end-to-end logit delta between the two quantizers is logged but **not** gated. A
swapped model is chaotic: after ~30 layers, two quantizers that agree to the last
representable code still move the max logit by O(1), so that number cannot separate a
real fault from arithmetic ordering.

`master_bf16`, `hf_bitnet` and `mask_sign` are re-read from disk. The GGUF/I2_S containers
have no in-tree reader, so they are gated *as they are packed*: each tensor's serialized
byte string is decoded again with our own unpacker and compared to the master's codes and
`s16` before the container writer sees it, and the digests land in
`ternary_block_gate.json` beside the file. `mask_sign` gets both — its bytes are gated as
they are packed (digests in `ternary_mask_sign.json`) *and* the written artifact is re-read
and compared. `onebitllms_bf16` stores a latent rather than a grid, so its gate re-runs
the consumer's own quantizer over the written tensors: the codes must come back exactly,
and the scale it re-derives must sit within 1% of the master's — which is what turns the
raw-master mistake into a failed export instead of a 0.68x shrink. A format with neither
gate is refused rather than written unverified.

A failing gate raises rather than writing a broken artifact.

## What not to quantize {#sensitive-modules}

The plugin hard-excludes the modules where ternarization is fatal, and `strict_enumeration`
turns every unrecognized module into a loud error instead of silent damage. Beyond those,
sensitivity is graded — this section is the field guide.

**Always full precision, not configurable:** token embeddings, `lm_head`, and every norm
gain. Ternary embeddings destroy a model outright (bitnet.cpp's own ablations), and norm
vectors are too small to be worth a scale. Exports keep them bf16/f16, optionally `Q8_0`
(`embedding_dtype: int8`), which is near-lossless.

**MoE routers stay FP forever.** A router is the one tensor where quantization noise
changes the computation graph: a flipped top-k pick routes tokens through different
experts entirely. The config validator carries router canary names so an unanchored
`.*gate.*` regex is rejected before it can ternarize `mlp.gate`, and fused 3-D expert
stacks are refused until the expert-aware path lands.

**Sensitivity is not uniform across the block.** An eval-only `axolotl ternary damage-map`
run on SmolLM2-135M ranks the families: `down_proj` is catastrophic alone (ppl 4e10),
`o_proj` severe (15k), `gate/up_proj` heavy (2--6k), `q/k/v_proj` mild (200--400). This is
exactly where BitDistill inserts SubLN and where BitNet-2B-4T carries `ffn_sub_norm` /
`attn_sub_norm`. Two recipes follow:

```yaml
# quality-critical at 1.58-bit: spend FP on the worst offender
ternary:
  keep_fp_modules:
    - '.*\.mlp\.down_proj'
```

Run the damage map on *your* model before choosing — the ranking above is one model at one
size, and the table is the whole point of the command.

**Gotchas without guardrails yet:**

- **MoE shared experts** are always-active and behave like a dense MLP — do not assume the
  "experts are ternarizable" logic covers them; keep them FP (or `dual`) until measured.
  Per-expert router bias terms (aux-loss-free routing) must stay FP.
- **Cold routed experts erode under weight decay**: decay fires every step whether or not
  an expert was routed, so rarely-used experts shrink monotonically into the zero-code
  region — dead experts that look like router collapse. Until gradient-gated decay masking
  lands, set expert weight decay to 0 on MoE conversions.
- **First and last decoder layers** are the classic mixed-precision escape hatches (raw
  embedding ingestion, head feeding). `keep_fp_modules: ['model\.layers\.0\..*']` is a
  cheap experiment when the damage map shows early-layer concentration.
- **Multimodal towers and hybrid-arch mixers** (vision encoders, Mamba/SSM in-projections,
  speech convs) have no presets on purpose: strict enumeration errors on them, forcing an
  explicit `keep_fp_modules` decision. Prism kept its vision tower at 4-bit, not ternary —
  treat that as the precedent.
- **Tiny projections** (aggressive GQA `k/v_proj`, low-rank adapters folded into bases)
  give the per-tensor scale very few weights to average over; if the damage map flags
  them, `learnable` scales usually recover it.

## Running the artifacts {#deployment}

What actually consumes each export, with commands. The short version: ternary kernels
live in the CPU ecosystem today (llama.cpp, bitnet.cpp); GPU serving stacks have no
ternary backend yet, and the two-plane modes ship as masters only.

| | llama.cpp / ollama | bitnet.cpp | transformers | vLLM / SGLang | MLX |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `master_bf16` | via convert (bf16) | — | ✓ (bf16) | ✓ (bf16, no size/speed win) | ✓ via 2-bit convert |
| `hf_bitnet` | — | — | ✓ packed | ✗ | — |
| `gguf_tq2_0` | ✓ (recommended) | — | — | ✗ | — |
| `gguf_tq1_0` | ✓ (smallest) | — | — | ✗ | — |
| `i2_s` | — | ✓ | — | ✗ | — |
| `mask_sign` | — | — | — | — | — |
| `dual` / `trit_planes` master | — | — | ✓ (bf16 values) | ✓ (bf16) | — |

### llama.cpp (and Ollama)

`TQ2_0` is the deployment default: ~2× `Q4_K` decode speed on AVX2 CPUs at 2.06 bpw.
`TQ1_0` trades some speed for the smallest footprint (1.69 bpw). Both are CPU-first
types — GPU/Metal offload for TQ tensors is limited upstream, so benchmark before
assuming an offloaded speedup; plan for CPU/edge serving.

```bash
axolotl ternary export config.yaml --format gguf_tq2_0
llama-cli -m outputs/model/gguf/model-tq2_0.gguf -p "..."   # or llama-server
```

With `ternary.export.embedding_dtype: int8` the embeddings/head emit as `Q8_0`, which
llama.cpp consumes natively and which roughly halves the unembedding DRAM traffic that
dominates single-stream decode. Ollama loads the same file through a `Modelfile`
(`FROM ./model-tq2_0.gguf`) on any build whose bundled llama.cpp is recent enough to
carry the TQ types.

### bitnet.cpp

Microsoft's dedicated ternary CPU runtime — the best published CPU throughput and
energy numbers for this format class (2.4–6.2× over llama.cpp on x86 in their report).
Export `i2_s`, then point their tooling at it:

```bash
axolotl ternary export config.yaml --format i2_s
python setup_env.py -md /path/to/export --quant-type i2_s   # in microsoft/BitNet
python run_inference.py -m ... -p "..."
```

### transformers

`hf_bitnet` loads directly on llama-family architectures — the packed uint8 weights and
`quantization_config` follow the upstream BitNet convention:

```python
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("outputs/model/hf_bitnet")
```

This is the correctness/eval path, not a speed path: transformers has no fused ternary
kernels, so it runs at bf16-class speed with packed-size memory. The `master_bf16`
loads anywhere transformers runs and stays re-finetunable.

### vLLM and SGLang

Neither has a ternary quantization backend today — the packed formats cannot be served.
The `master_bf16` serves as an ordinary bf16 model (full memory, no speedup), which is
useful for quality evaluation behind an OpenAI-compatible API rather than efficiency.
Watch upstream for TQ/BitNet backend support before planning GPU serving around ternary.

### MLX (Apple Silicon)

MLX has no scale-only ternary type, but a ternary master quantizes **exactly** into
MLX's affine 2-bit group format: every group's values are a subset of `{-s, 0, +s}`, so
the affine fit is lossless (this is also how Prism ships its ternary models on MLX).

```bash
mlx_lm.convert --hf-path outputs/model -q --q-bits 2 --q-group-size 64
```

Verify with a fixed-prompt logits comparison against the master after converting — the
exactness argument holds per group, but embedding/head quantization settings differ by
mlx-lm version.

### Two-plane modes and what is missing

`dual` and `trit_planes` masters currently run only as bf16 models (ternary-family
quality at bf16 memory) — no engine has five- or nine-level kernels. The path to
deploying them is an FV5-style bit-plane format plus a llama.cpp fork carrying its
kernels, which is the top item on this plugin's roadmap given how strongly those modes
outperform single-plane at equal healing budget. `mask_sign` is archival/transport
only. For extra CPU headroom on the GGUF artifacts, T-MAC's LUT kernels consume
low-bit GGUF files and post 4–5× single-thread gains over llama.cpp in their paper —
an advanced option, not a supported target of this plugin's gates.

## Damage map {#damage-map}

Before spending a heal budget, measure what the quantizer actually costs *this* model:

```bash
axolotl ternary damage-map config.yaml
axolotl ternary damage-map config.yaml --num-sequences 128 --sequence-len 2048
axolotl ternary damage-map config.yaml --dataset wikitext --json
```

It loads the FP model, swaps it as a training run would (minus `init` and `subln`, which
are not function-preserving at λ=0 and would move the baseline), and runs eval-only passes
over a small split of your own corpus — no training, no optimizer, no checkpoints written.
The split is read as **raw text**: it tokenizes a `text` / `content` / `raw_content` field
and never applies a prompt strategy, so point `--dataset` at a pretraining-style corpus if
your `datasets:` are instruction records.

```
64 sequences x 1024 tokens

scope               perplexity         delta
--------------------------------------------
baseline                9.8412
weights                24.6031      +14.7619
activations            10.9902       +1.1490
both                   26.4188      +16.5776
family:q_proj          10.1044       +0.2632
family:down_proj       14.9077       +5.0665
```

- **`weights`** — ternary weights, full-precision activations.
- **`activations`** — FP weights, per-token int8 activations (measured whatever
  `activation_bits` says, so the row is comparable across configs).
- **`both`** — the configured quantizer.
- **`family:<name>`** — that family ternary, every other module full precision, and no
  activation quantization anywhere — the same axis as the `weights` row, so the two
  compare.

How to read it: weight-dominant damage is what a fitted `init` and a longer λ warmup buy
down. Activation-dominant damage is not — that is the case for `activation_bits: null` or
(once implemented) `smoothing`. A single family far above the others is a candidate for
`keep_fp_modules`; `down_proj` and `o_proj` are the usual offenders, which is also why
`subln` puts its norms in front of exactly those two.

Perplexity here is a *relative* instrument. Run it on a few hundred sequences of the corpus
you intend to heal on and compare rows within one table, not across models or splits.

## Relationship to `use_onebitllms`

| | `ternary` plugin | `use_onebitllms` |
|---|---|---|
| Input | any supported FP checkpoint | an already-prequantized BitNet checkpoint (Falcon-E) |
| Job | convert FP → ternary, then heal | fine-tune weights that are already ternary |
| Cost | billions of tokens of continued training | an ordinary fine-tune |
| Export | built in (`axolotl ternary export`) | external `onebitllms` CLI |

They cannot be combined; the config validator rejects it. Pick conversion if you have an
FP model you want to shrink, and `use_onebitllms` if someone already did the shrinking.

## FAQ

**Why is LoRA / QLoRA not supported?**
Ternary conversion moves roughly 40% of the weights — that is the entire point of the
"reconstruction" regime. A low-rank update cannot express that, and there is nothing for
an adapter to wrap: the quantized weight is a function of the latent weight, which has to
be trainable. Full fine-tuning is not an implementation shortcut here, it is the method.

**Why do `lm_head` and the embeddings stay full precision?**
They are the most quantization-sensitive tensors in the model and ternarizing them
collapses output quality, which is why every deployment format keeps them at higher
precision (GGUF uses Q6_K/F16). They are also a small fraction of a multi-billion-parameter
model's weights, so the compression you give up is minor.

**Why is there no ternary backward pass?**
Straight-through estimation means gradients and optimizer state live on the full-precision
latent weights. The forward is ternary; the backward is dense bf16 by design. A ternary
backward would have nothing to accumulate into.

**Can I skip the λ warmup?**
`lambda_schedule: none` quantizes at full strength from step 0. It is available, and for
very small models it makes little difference, but on pretrained models of meaningful size
a hard jump to λ=1 causes catastrophic forgetting the run never recovers from.

**Does `int8_forward` change the numerics?**
It is gated on λ == 1, where the effective weights are exactly `code · s`, and is verified
against the eager reference implementation. It is a speed path, not a different quantizer;
`auto` falls back to the fake-quant path whenever shapes or hardware do not qualify.

**Which architectures work?**
Presets ship for `llama` and `qwen3` dense models, and the export writers target those
families first. Other architectures can be converted by supplying `target_modules`
explicitly, but the GGUF/bitnet.cpp writers need per-architecture tensor-name mapping and
will tell you when they do not have it. Fused 3D MoE expert stacks are detected and
rejected with a clear error rather than silently mishandled.

## Example configurations

See `examples/ternary/`:

- `llama-3.2-1b-qat.yaml` — pure QAT heal on streamed pretraining text.
- `qwen3-4b-distill.yaml` — the same heal with an in-process frozen FP teacher.
- `llama-3.2-1b-ptq-init.yaml` — calibrated PTQ init, KD anchored to the LR-decay tail, and
  a `mask_sign` export; pair it with `axolotl ternary damage-map`.
